title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: A rough audience recording that struggles with clarity but still delivers a lively free‑concert vibe highlighted by strong Good Lovin' and Lovelight moments.
ai_review.review: The tape is an audience capture – far from a soundboard – with noticeable hiss, crowd din and occasional drop‑outs, making many parts hard to hear.  Nonetheless listeners praise the energy of the show, especially the electric jams on “Good Lovin’”, “Lovelight”, and the surprising renditions of “Hard To Handle” and the China/Rider sequence.  The historic free concert atmosphere shines through despite the audio shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Show performance is generally praised with several standout songs, but recording quality is widely criticized as poor to only fair, pulling the overall rating down.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners describe it as a back‑pocket crowd tape with heavy din, hiss and occasional clarity (e.g., Lovelight). Not soundboard quality; many parts are buried under audience noise.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Free concert with an acoustic Garcia/Weir opener, New Riders set, then the Dead.  The show carries a historic protest vibe (post‑Cambodia bombing) and a laid‑back hilltop atmosphere.
